deep.reconstruction:
The page is a structured plan for a chapter titled 'Espaces de Schatten'. It develops what are now called symmetrically normed operator ideals.

(1) Sequence spaces (normes de Schatten).
- A Schatten norm is a symmetric gauge function N on finitely supported sequences: a norm invariant under permutations, depending only on the moduli |λ_i|, and normalized so that N(e_1)=1. Examples are the ℓ^p norms N_p.
- N is extended to all of C^ℕ with values in [0,∞], via sup over finite sections.
- ℓ^N = {x : N(x)<∞} is the maximal space. ℓ_N is the closure of the finitely supported sequences C^(ℕ) in ℓ^N, the minimal (separable) space.
- Normalization gives N_∞ ≤ N ≤ N_1, hence ℓ^1 ⊂ ℓ^N ⊂ ℓ^∞ and ℓ^1 ⊂ ℓ_N ⊂ c_0.
- Proposition: the maximal space lies in c_0 unless N is equivalent to N_∞. The reason: if ℓ^N contains a non-null sequence, symmetry and monotonicity force (1,1,1,…) into ℓ^N, so N ≤ C·N_∞.
- Polarity: N° is the dual gauge, N°(y) = sup{|Σ x_i y_i| : N(x) ≤ 1}, and (N°)° = N.
- Duality: (ℓ_N)' = ℓ^{N°}. Corollary: ℓ^N and ℓ_N are complete (Banach).
- Reflexivity: ℓ_N reflexive ⇔ ℓ^N reflexive ⇔ ℓ_{N°} reflexive ⇔ ℓ^{N°} reflexive ⇔ (ℓ_N = ℓ^N and ℓ_{N°} = ℓ^{N°}).
- Example: (N_p)° = N_{p'}, which recovers the reflexivity of ℓ^p for 1<p<∞.

(2) Operator ideals (espaces de Schatten), for Hilbert spaces E, F.
- For compact u ∈ L_0(E,F), set N(u) = N((λ_i(u))), with λ_i the singular values.
- Duality formula: N(u) = sup{|Tr(uw)| : w ∈ F'⊗E finite rank, N°(w) ≤ 1}.
- This formula is taken as the definition of N(u) for arbitrary bounded u ∈ L(E,F). Then L^N(E,F) = {u : N(u)<∞} is a normed space (the maximal ideal, cf. Gohberg–Krein S_Φ). L_N(E,F) is the closure of E'⊗F in it (the minimal ideal S_Φ^(0)).
- Proposition: u ∈ L_N ⇔ u compact and (λ_i(u)) ∈ ℓ_N.
- Inclusions: L^1 ⊂ L^N ⊂ L, and L^1 ⊂ L_N ⊂ L_0.
- Ideal and symmetry properties: N(u)=N(u*), N(vu) ≤ ‖v‖N(u), N(uw) ≤ ‖w‖N(u). By the sup formula these reduce to the compact case, where they follow from λ_i(vu) ≤ ‖v‖λ_i(u).

Purpose and context. The previous page gives the intrinsic characterization: unitarily invariant cross norms on E'⊗F correspond to symmetric gauge functions. The next page proves L^N ⊂ L_0 unless N ~ N_∞, gives trace duality (L_N)' = L^{N°}, reflexivity of L^p, and a Hölder-type inequality N(vu) ≤ N'(u)N''(v). This is the Hilbert-space model case for Grothendieck's tensor-product/operator-ideal programme (cf. Schatten's 1950 cross-spaces).
errors: The proposition 'l_N ⊂ c_0 sauf si N est équivalente à N_∞' is wrong as written for the minimal space. ℓ_N ⊂ c_0 always, since N ≥ N_∞ (and he lists ℓ_N ⊂ c_0 two lines above). The intended statement must be ℓ^N ⊂ c_0 unless N ~ N_∞, which is the sequence analogue of the next page's 'L^N(E,F) ⊂ L_0(E,F) si N non équivalente à N_∞'.

The direction of the inclusions under 'N' ≤ N''' looks reversed under the usual ordering of norms. If N' ≤ N'' pointwise, then N''(x)<∞ implies N'(x)<∞, so ℓ^{N''} ⊂ ℓ^{N'}. Grothendieck writes ℓ^{N'} ⊂ ℓ^{N''} and L^{N'} ⊂ L^{N''}. This is consistent only if the order is meant as N' ≥ N'' (e.g. N_1 ≥ N ≥ N_∞ giving ℓ^1 ⊂ ℓ^N ⊂ ℓ^∞). It is a slip or a non-standard convention.
The machine transcription reads '(N°)° = N°'. This should be (N°)° = N (bipolar).

ideas.what: Symmetric gauge functions on sequences, the maximal and minimal sequence spaces ℓ^N and ℓ_N, and their duality (ℓ_N)' = ℓ^{N°}
ideas.modern_name: Symmetric sequence spaces / symmetric gauge functions and their Köthe duals
ideas.where_published: Possibly touched on in Produits tensoriels topologiques (1955), not as a systematic treatment

ideas.what: Maximal space contained in c_0 unless N ~ N_∞
ideas.modern_name: S_Φ ⊂ compact operators unless Φ is equivalent to the sup norm

ideas.what: Reflexivity criterion: ℓ_N reflexive iff ℓ_N = ℓ^N and ℓ_{N°} = ℓ^{N°}, with the operator analogue
ideas.modern_name: Reflexivity of symmetric sequence spaces and symmetrically normed ideals (both the space and its dual are separable / order continuous)

ideas.what: Defining N(u) for arbitrary bounded u by sup |Tr uw| over finite-rank w with N°(w) ≤ 1, giving the maximal ideal L^N and the minimal ideal L_N
ideas.modern_name: Maximal and minimal symmetrically normed ideals S_Φ, S_Φ^(0) via trace duality

ideas.what: Ideal property via the singular value inequality λ_i(vu) ≤ ‖v‖λ_i(u), and N(u)=N(u*)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clean, contemporaneous (1953) outline of the theory of symmetrically normed ideals, parallel to Schatten's 1950 work. It anticipates the Gohberg–Krein (1965) presentation: maximal versus minimal ideals, trace duality, and the reflexivity criterion. Historically it is a nice example of Grothendieck's independent systematization. Mathematically, everything here is standard and was published by others; nothing appears missing from the literature.
transcription_corrections: 'Corollaire l^N est [?] ..., l_N est complet' is likely 'Corollaire: l^N et l_N sont complets' (cf. next page, Corollaire 1).
'Prop l_N ⊂ c_0 sauf si N est équivalente à N_∞' is a mathematical slip in the manuscript rather than a transcription error; the intended statement is probably l^N.
In the definition of N(u), the sup is over w ∈ F'⊗E with N°(w) ≤ 1. The crossed-out/overwritten 'N(w)' under the sup is a correction artifact; the dual norm N° is intended.
'Corollaire l^N est [?]' line: 'Polarité' is followed by the bipolar identity, and 'Prop le dual de l_N est l^{N°}' is correct as transcribed.
